title: INTEGRATED MASTER PLAN FOR RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE
body_text:
Under its broad policy framework, Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) has been undertaking various targeted interventions for integrated and sustainable development rural areas of the country. With the main focus on infrastructure development, increasing livelihood opportunities, empowering rural women and expanding livelihood opportunities, MoRD is implementing Pradhan Mantri Gram SadakYojana(PMGSY), Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar&Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) and DeendayalAntyodayaYojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) across the country including Bhind and Datia districts of Madhya Pradesh. As per the implementation framework of the programmes, States/UTs are conceiving the project proposals for infrastructure including roads and sustainable assets, identification of beneficiary, generation of demand for employment, livelihood programmes, keeping in view the actual requirement of interventions for improving the quality of life of rural population. The above programmes are implemented in convergence with various central and state schemes to optimize the pace of rural development in the country. However, at present, there is no proposal in this Ministry for an integrated master plan for rural infrastructure and livelihood development for each LokSabha Constituency.
MoRD has evolved a comprehensive multilevel and multi format system of periodic assessment and review of progress and outcome of its rural development schemes, through Performance Review Committee Meetings, National Level Monitors (NLMs), Area Officers Schemes, Common Review Mission, Mid-Term Review, Labour Budget meetings, Labour Budget Revision meetings, Programme Review meetings, Concurrent Evaluation and Impact Assessment Studies. Specific reviews of States/UTs are also undertaken from time to time and action is taken on the basis of their findings. In addition, MoRD constitutes District Level Development Coordination and Monitoring Committees (DISHA) under the chairpersonship of the respective Members of Parliament to foster better coordination among elected representatives of Parliament, State Legislatures, and Local Governments (Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies) to ensure the effective and timely implementation of key Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes including the schemes/programmes of MoRD at district level.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
***
RC/PU

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply dated 11 August 2026, Minister of State for Rural Development Shri Kamlesh Paswan stated that MoRD implements PMGSY, Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar & Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), and DAY-NRLM across the country, including Bhind and Datia districts of Madhya Pradesh, to improve rural infrastructure, employment and livelihoods. He clarified that there is currently no proposal for a separate integrated master plan for rural infrastructure and livelihood development for each Lok Sabha Constituency. The reply also detailed the Ministry's multi-layered monitoring architecture, including Performance Review Committees, National Level Monitors, Common Review Missions, and DISHA committees chaired by MPs at the district level.
enrichment.context:
This reply reflects the Ministry of Rural Development's ongoing strategy of implementing flagship schemes—PMGSY (rural road connectivity since 2000), MGNREGA-linked employment guarantee programmes (rebranded here as VB-G RAM G), and DAY-NRLM (women's self-help group-based livelihoods mission)—in convergence with state schemes rather than through a single unified plan per constituency. The DISHA (District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee) mechanism, established via a 2016 government resolution, is significant for exam purposes as it institutionalizes MP-led oversight of Centrally Sponsored Schemes at the district level, bridging the gap between Parliament, state legislatures, and Panchayati Raj Institutions.

The clarification that no LS-constituency-specific master plan exists is notable given periodic demands (often raised in Parliament) for constituency-level infrastructure planning to ensure equitable resource distribution. It underscores the government's continued reliance on scheme-based, state-driven project proposal mechanisms (bottom-up demand generation) rather than top-down constituency mapping, which has implications for debates on decentralized planning and the effectiveness of MPLADS-type mechanisms versus scheme convergence.

prelims_questions.question: The 'DISHA' committees mentioned in the context of monitoring rural development schemes are chaired by which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: As stated in the release, District Level Development Coordination and Monitoring Committees (DISHA) are chaired by the respective Members of Parliament to foster coordination among various levels of elected representatives and local governments.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following schemes/missions is primarily associated with empowering rural women through Self-Help Groups?
options: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar & Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
prelims_questions.explanation: DAY-NRLM, referenced in the release as one of MoRD's key programmes, is specifically focused on organizing rural women into Self-Help Groups to enhance livelihood opportunities and empowerment.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role and effectiveness of institutional mechanisms like DISHA committees in ensuring coordinated implementation of centrally sponsored rural development schemes at the district level.

Examine the rationale behind scheme-based convergence approaches versus constituency-specific master planning for rural infrastructure development in India. What are the merits and limitations of each approach?
